title: Conservation of energy (power balance)
references: Callen, H. B., Thermodynamics and an Introduction to Thermostatistics, 2nd ed., Wiley (1985)
Feynman, R. P., Leighton, R. B. and Sands, M., The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Vol. I, chapter 4, Addison-Wesley (1963)
validity_domain: A device in steady state whose only source of energy is the stated input power cannot deliver more output power than it takes in (first law of thermodynamics).
limitations: Assumption energy_sources: when the input is the only energy source, output power is at most the input power; when other sources exist (fuel, stored energy, ambient heat for a heat pump) this law gives no bound; the engine needs a finite number, so 1e30 times the input power stands for no bound.
Steady state: a device may release stored energy for a short time
Output and input are compared in the same unit of power

variables.P_in: Input power, the device's only energy source
